# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 18 | **Condition:** heavily damaged

---

**18:1** [...] for the wicked [...] snares of evil [...]

**18:2** [...] in their scheming circle they plotted against me [...]

**18:3** [...] they bricked up every source of understanding and kept the water of knowledge locked away.

**18:4** And for the thirsty [...] they stare at their own foolishness [...]

**18:5** [...] at their celebrations [...] for they set up [...]

**18:6** [...] they drove me out of my homeland the way a bird is flushed from its nest,

**18:7** and every companion and friend I ever had was torn away from me.

**18:8** They look at me like a smashed jar. These spinners of lies and counterfeit visionaries --

**18:9** they hatched a wicked plot against me, a Belial scheme, to rip out Your teaching,

**18:10** the one You carved on my heart, and swap it for easy answers for Your people.

**18:11** They starved the thirsty of real knowledge, and when they begged for water

**18:12** they poured them vinegar instead. [...] their wickedness [...]

**18:13** [...] the gates of pain slammed shut with no way out [...] weapons of war [...]

**18:14** [...] a bar crushing my bones [...] like a ship in the fury of [...]

**18:15** [...] they rage like ocean breakers. [...] advisors schooled in treachery [...]

**18:16** [...] the plot [...] closing in on me like a siege.

**18:17** My soul inside me is failing [...] all the strength has drained from my body,

**18:18** my heart is spilling out like water, my flesh is melting away like wax,

**18:19** the power in my legs has turned to raw fear, my arm has been ripped from its socket.

**18:20** I cannot [...] for the hostility has no cure, and accusation burns [...]

**18:21** [...] I cannot [...] my pain [...] a sickness unto death [...]

**18:22** [...] but they [...] they celebrate [...] piling on [...]

**18:23** [...] my arm [...] my foot sinks deeper into the mud.

**18:24** [...] the snares of wickedness have surrounded me [...] and nets [...]

**18:25** But You, God, [...] You tucked my soul into the bundle of life,

**18:26** and You shielded me from every trap set by the pit. Violent men

**18:27** hunted for my life, but they never won because You braced my heart

**18:28** and rushed to my side. Through Your faithful love [...] and the flood of Your mercy

**18:29** You steadied my footing, and in the magnitude of Your pardon [...] You refused to discard me,

**18:30** and when my soul was in the worst of its anguish You did not walk away.

**18:31** [...] my cry [...] You answered my groans with a word of comfort,

**18:32** and I found joy in forgiveness, and I was consoled about the sin that came before.

**18:33** I know that hope lives in Your faithful love and confidence lives in the abundance of Your power,

**18:34** for nobody walks free without Your approval, and nobody [...] apart from Your will.

**18:35** [...] You teach all knowledge, and everything that exists does so because You willed it.

**18:36** No one else can respond to Your design, no one can understand

**18:37** all Your holy purpose or look into the depths of Your secrets or take in the full scope of Your wonders.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Column 18 is badly damaged but the surviving material is devastating -- a person being physically and socially destroyed, enemies gloating, body falling apart. And then the turn: "You tucked my soul into the bundle of life." The poet's movement from desolation to consolation is the emotional core of the Hodayot.*
